title: Check: rollouts and rollbacks
description: Five questions on rolling updates, surge and rollback.

questions.prompt: Which update strategy does a Deployment use by default?
questions.explanation: RollingUpdate replaces Pods gradually so the app stays available. Recreate deletes them all first and is only right when two versions must never run at once.

questions.prompt: `maxSurge: 1` and `maxUnavailable: 0` on a 3-replica Deployment means what?

options.text: At most 2 Pods run during the rollout
Up to 4 Pods may run, and 3 stay available throughout
One Pod is deleted before any is created
The rollout is paused after one Pod

questions.explanation: maxSurge adds capacity above the desired count; maxUnavailable 0 means none of the existing three may go away before a replacement is ready.

questions.prompt: Write the command that rolls a Deployment named api back to its previous revision.
questions.explanation: Old ReplicaSets are kept precisely so a rollback is just a scale-up of the previous one.

questions.prompt: Write the command that lists the revision history of that Deployment.
questions.explanation: `revisionHistoryLimit` controls how many old ReplicaSets are retained and therefore how far back you can roll.

questions.prompt: A rollout is stuck and `kubectl rollout status` never returns. Where do you look first?

options.text: `kubectl describe pod` on a new Pod, for the events

questions.explanation: A stuck rollout almost always means the new Pods will not become ready - image pull failure, failing probe or unschedulable. The events say which.
